## Practical numerical precision

For practical numerical software, start with the lowest arithmetic precision that
plausibly serves the application on the actual hardware. Optimize useful
end-to-end capacity on challenging supported workloads and prevent backlog or
deadline failure. Higher precision must earn its cost through a demonstrated
practical benefit or an explicit requirement; promote only the affected operations
or state. Compare complete algorithms, including preparation, conversion,
transfers and synchronization: a higher-precision algorithm can win by doing less
work.

Automatic mode is the user's maximum-useful-processing option. Choose the route
that provides the better challenging-case ceiling across its supported range; do
not wait for backlog, require manual per-stage tuning, or let a negligible
easy-case latency/power advantage set a lower-capacity global default when no
such user objective exists. Respect declared resource ceilings and real latency
requirements. Use headroom for useful search, trials, scene complexity or other
requested work, not empty utilization. Preserve a simple higher-precision/minimum-
precision override, capability dispatch and explicit fallback reporting.

Judge precision by practical outcomes, not automatic agreement with FP64, ADC bit
depth, or an invented universal ppm/dB cutoff. Preserve failed diagnostics and
distinguish their source from binding contracts. Report proportionate
quality/capacity tradeoffs and uncertainty. Keep exact counters and explicit output
requirements exact. Distinguish storage, multiplication and accumulation precision
and actual executed instructions. When credible hardware evidence predicts an
unrealized low-precision gain, check dispatch, packing, shapes, conversion and
complete-stage cost before dismissing the opportunity. A tiny neutral test does
not settle demanding-case potential; an advertised peak does not qualify a route.
Use bounded representative experiments, then implement and automatically select
supported improvements within authorization.

Apply this default to modems, measurement appliances, simulations, rendering,
games and other practical numerical applications. Evaluate reception, false
alarms, completed design trials, useful scene complexity or the actual product
outcome. Numerical error against a reference is a diagnostic unless the applicable
contract makes it an acceptance condition. Neither "preserve accuracy" nor an
existing `double` type establishes a scientific-precision requirement. An
explicit scientific, exactness or other output contract remains binding; do not
silently weaken it. Normalize or scale data, use wider accumulators or retain
sensitive coordinates/state where they demonstrate a practical benefit instead
of promoting the whole pipeline. Fewer bits alone do not guarantee faster work.

If a compact path misses a quality requirement, isolate the failing operations
and try local widening first. Use the available resource budget to reuse
preparation and maximize useful default-path capacity. Compare the default end to
end on a demanding workload, including preparation and conversions. Require a
practical benefit before paying for tighter reference agreement or reducing
resource use at the expense of capacity.

Treat storage and executed arithmetic as separate choices. Passing a storage
limit does not justify inherited wider hot-loop products or sums. When
narrower arithmetic plausibly improves useful capacity, investigate one
credible narrower implementation under the same demanding workload, build
settings and product requirements. Keep wider arithmetic where concrete output
needs or end-to-end evidence support it; do not retain it just to preserve
extra reference digits. Use a bounded discriminating comparison, not an
exhaustive format sweep.

Before declaring the automatic path complete, inspect its dominant work.
Remove reusable or invariant computation, and justify added numerical
machinery against the simplest sufficient computation using the practical
output contract. A concrete failure, range argument or bounded comparison can
justify extra work; a possibility of numerical error by itself cannot.

An algorithmic improvement does not by itself justify the arithmetic precision
chosen inside the replacement algorithm. For its main numerical computation,
qualify one plausible narrower implementation or give a concrete output
requirement for the wider choice. When qualified choices are effectively tied,
prefer narrower arithmetic; retain wider arithmetic for a demonstrated
practical benefit.

Treat completion of substantive numerical changes as proposed until an
independent reviewer checks the practical numerical decisions and observable
reports. The reviewer traces executed operand, product, accumulation and
conversion types through the main loops, verifies useful work, demanding
defaults, overrides and resource accounting, and investigates one credible
consequential gap with a bounded check. Relay evidenced findings to the owner
for repair and re-review without asking the user to tune internal stages.
Preserve original attempts and distinguish owner results from independently
accepted results. Reuse the existing review-and-repair process; delegated
reviews do not recursively request another review.

For a numerical acceptance assignment, reuse the existing independent review
and owner-repair roles. Supply the actual task, source, public evidence, numerical
guidance, read/write scope and aggregate budget. The following review questions
belong in that assignment; map paths to the real scope instead of requiring a
particular directory layout:

- Trace executed operand, multiplication, accumulation and conversion types
  through each main numerical loop, including implicit promotions and library
  overloads. A narrow destination or buffer does not establish narrow computation.
- Check the practical justification for retained wider hot arithmetic and added
  numerical machinery, including inside replacement algorithms. Verify complete
  useful work, invariant preparation, demanding automatic/default requests, exact
  state, supported overrides and truthful accounting for live allocations.
- Investigate one credible consequential gap when supplied evidence is
  insufficient, using a bounded check and end-to-end cost where performance
  matters. Do not invent a higher precision requirement, speed ratio, particular
  algorithm or exhaustive optimization requirement. Preserve uncertainty.
- Return acceptance or specific evidenced findings to the owner. The owner
  repairs the production source; the independent reviewer checks the affected
  contracts. Preserve original attempts, repair rounds, budgets and role limits.
  Do not present a reviewed-and-repaired result as one-shot worker success.

This is instruction-level guidance using the existing review-and-repair process,
not a new runtime interception or proof of compliance. A delegated review does
not recursively invoke another review or the main-chat completion gate.

End-user and experiment turnaround time are part of the objective. Start with a
small discriminating check using the production implementation, reusing valid
evidence. Sample demanding shapes and relevant failure cases rather than relying
only on an easy demonstration. Report quality/capacity tradeoffs instead of
inventing a universal allowable loss. Identify actual supported dispatch and
fallback scope; a promising candidate can merit implementation and qualification
without being ready for automatic deployment. Avoid exhaustive per-stage sweeps
when a bounded comparison can settle the choice.

[FP16 guidance](https://gpuopen.com/learn/first-steps-implementing-fp16/) shows why

[WMMA documentation](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.3.0/cuda-programming-guide/05-appendices/cpp-language-extensions.html)
documents supported operand/accumulator combinations. These support implementation

the current target's capabilities and execution path.

## Native numerical processing

For modems, DSP, and other intensive numerical processing inside an existing
native application, **default to C++ or a similarly integrated native approach**.
Prefer improving the current implementation, using appropriate native libraries,
or adding a compatible in-process native component before moving part of the
production hot path into Python scripts or separate processes. Familiarity with
Python, shorter code, or a quick isolated prototype is not sufficient reason to
introduce that architectural split. This is an application-integration preference,
not a requirement to rewrite successful Python applications or the kit's Python
orchestration tools.

Honor stricter project contracts. Where the project requires one canonical
compiled DSP and persistent receiver-state implementation, generic allowances
for Python experiments or libraries do not authorize a second implementation
or a Python-owned operating stage. Extend the native interfaces and probes;
Python can launch them and analyze results. A separate C++ operating process
still introduces a process boundary. Conversely, fresh native probe processes
for test isolation do not split the application's operating signal chain.

The user's November 10, 2026 engineering retrospective reported that diverting
part of a C++ signal-processing chain into Python caused considerable agent
distraction and integration difficulty. In that experience:

- Returning to C++ made it easier to restructure multithreading and overlap
  parallel processing of one batch with less parallel preparation of the next.
- Managing separate processes instead of internal threads appeared to reduce
  utilization and complicate coordination.
- Separate Python scripts made GPU testing on cloud RunPod instances harder
  than the native binary workflow; suitable tensor-core paths may also have
  received less investigation.
- Integrating a second signal-processing chain that narrowed the first chain's
  work became harder across inter-process communication boundaries.

These are reported project lessons, not controlled language benchmarks. The
pumpModem activity and validation record reviewed on November 10 (revision
`89945e8`) qualify the account: a later native scheduler improved first-message
latency but worsened first-slot latency and slightly
increased total replay time versus an earlier native baseline; it did not
establish a general throughput or utilization gain. Native GPU optimizations
improved scoped stages, while the small FP16 experiment was slower with packing
costs and useful Tensor Core acceleration remained unproven. Preserve these
distinctions: easier integration exposes optimization opportunities, but a
language change, more concurrency or a fast kernel does not prove a faster
complete receiver.

Before proposing a split, inspect the existing native pipeline and evaluate:

1. **Scheduling and utilization.** Identify serial preparation, parallel batch
   work and dependencies. Consider reusable thread pools, pipelining or double
   buffering to overlap preparation and computation, bounded queues and
   backpressure, and CPU/GPU overlap where useful. Check nested library threads
   and oversubscription. Coordinate stages within one explicit worker budget;
   smaller ready batches need not shrink the global allocation. Preserve ordered
   state/commit dependencies, cancellation and full memory reservations for
   overlapping work; retain ownership until cancelled work actually stops.
   Measure first-result latency, complete-message latency and sustained backlog
   service separately; extra concurrency or high utilization
   alone does not prove useful throughput. Project-specific worker multipliers
   and memory limits are not universal defaults.
2. **Data flow and chain coupling.** Keep compatible ownership and buffer
   lifetimes, minimize copies and synchronization, and let one chain's detections
   or candidate pruning reduce the other's work promptly. Transfer measurements
   with their uncertainty and validity bounds; retain a correct fallback when
   assistance is absent or invalid. Qualify each kind of assistance separately:
   pumpModem's reviewed Helper path supplies frequency intervals, not validated
   phase/timing transfer. Reducing the search work can matter more than making
   each operation faster. Account for latency, serialization, transfers,
   duplicated state and failure handling at each
   proposed process boundary. For example, Python's
   [multiprocessing queues serialize objects](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/multiprocessing.html#exchanging-objects-between-processes).
   Shared memory may reduce copies but still needs
   ownership and synchronization; an in-process binding differs from script IPC.
3. **GPU execution and reproducibility.** Design native CPU/GPU interfaces for
   useful batches, suitable contiguous layouts, explicit shapes/strides and
   reusable owned workspace. Qualify precision by stage: lower-precision bulk
   arithmetic can coexist with sensitive coordinates, accumulation or decisions
   needing higher precision. Arithmetic agreement alone does not qualify receiver
   acquisition or sensitivity; report fallback paths explicitly. Inspect launch,
   packing, transfer and synchronization costs before assuming tensor arithmetic
   addresses the bottleneck. Extend
   native probes around the production code instead of duplicating DSP in a
   convenient benchmark script that needs another port. Keep local, CI, manual
   and cloud tests such as RunPod on that same implementation, using a minimal
   native source closure, reproducible build, required libraries/drivers, inputs
   and launch instructions. Include setup and deployment effort when comparing
   approaches; a native binary still has dependencies.
4. **Evidence for an exception.** Compare a proposed alternative with a credible
   integrated native baseline on representative end-to-end work. Preserve
   required application outcomes under the
   [practical precision guidance](#practical-numerical-precision); measure latency, throughput, CPU/GPU
   utilization, memory and transfer/copy costs, and account for build/deployment
   reproducibility and maintenance effort. Include preparation, communication,
   synchronization and cross-chain work reduction. An isolated fast kernel does
   not establish a faster application. Label unmeasured benefits as hypotheses
   and use a bounded experiment before committing to a large rewrite.

When migrating an existing implementation, trace indirect test, CI, manual-case
and forecasting entry points as well as the application. A runner called
"native" may still measure retired code. Keep historical timings labeled with
their implementation and source identity; establish new baselines rather than
silently reusing old calibration. GPU-observed work or speed alone does not
establish CPU capacity: use source- and workload-matched local CPU calibration
and independent holdouts, retaining unresolved complete-receiver coverage.

Python remains useful for experiments, offline analysis, test harnesses,
orchestration, and bindings to optimized native libraries within the project's
contract. A Python component can be appropriate when existing architecture,
necessary libraries, isolation
requirements or measured end-to-end benefits justify it. Explain that reason
and the integration costs; prefer keeping tightly coupled production work
in-process when practical. This guidance does not authorize a language rewrite
or new deployment outside the user's task.

Do not assume Python prevents parallel native execution or tensor-core use, or
that C++ automatically enables either. Python numerical libraries can
[release the GIL for native work](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/thread_safety.html)
and [use tensor-core-backed GPU operations](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.15/notes/numerical_accuracy.html#tensorfloat-32-tf32-on-nvidia-ampere-and-later-devices).
Tensor acceleration depends on supported
operations, precision, shapes and the actual kernel/library path, with profiling
and numerical validation required for a performance claim. Apply the
[GPU selection and performance evidence](#gpu-selection-and-performance-evidence)
criteria in either language.

have been shown to the user, or may be unavailable in accessible records. Keep

operation-only restriction or a broader prohibition without evidence. Keep the

### Scientific literature research and development uptake

**Initiate substantial research when the development task warrants it, without
waiting for the user to ask for research or devote the main chat solely to it.**
Early in an ordinary scientific/numerical feature, audit or redesign, assess the
available grounding against the scope of the decisions ahead. If important
mechanisms, competing approach families, empirical assumptions or operating
conditions remain poorly understood and could materially change the work, the
coordinator initiates a dedicated research assignment; an assigned engineering
owner requests it through the existing coordinator channel. Do not leave this
recognition to the user's choice of boilerplate. If existing curated research
already supplies adequate depth, retrieve and apply it, verifying consequential
claims and current applicability; investigate its gaps instead of duplicating it.

Commission substantial new grounding as a standalone scientific assignment.
Start the brief with the scientific knowledge to develop and the reusable
scientific account to produce, comparable in depth to a dedicated main-chat
research task. Carry the complete development request, operating envelope,
constraints and relevant factual source as clearly labeled application context.
They remain binding, but the research actor does not own delivery or approval of
the implementation plan. The ordinary task owner derives this scientific brief
from the problem and evidence. Use a self-contained brief in a fresh context
through a supported route where available; do not assume that another agent
identity proves absent inherited context or isolation, or invent an unsupported
creation parameter. Preserve the actual delivery limits. Carry the whole
scientific problem through delegation: code audits and subject partitions do not
remove the lead's responsibility for links among mechanisms, observations,
inference, validation and computational feasibility. Transferred scientific
questions retain explicit owners and return evidence for integration.

When a broad consequential task needs substantial new scientific grounding, use
**two independent full-problem inquiries** through permitted scientific
responsibilities. Each receives the original problem, constraints and
common source facts, and owns a research-only account across that problem. Do not
divide the envelope between them or disclose the other inquiry's questions,
findings or an emerging engineering plan before their initial substantive
accounts are preserved. The owner sets an initial-account checkpoint within one
shared allowance and retains capacity for reconciliation and follow-through.
Specialist discovery can support either inquiry; it does not replace independent
full-problem explanations. The task owner commissions one pair for the overall
scientific problem; an assigned inquiry completes that scope and requests bounded
support, not another pair for the same problem. This conditional structure is for
substantial broad grounding, not routine questions or duplication of already
adequate research.

After preserving the independent full-problem discovery accounts, the research
lead derives a revisable outline of scientific subjects from the original problem
and inspected literature. For material subjects whose grounding is inadequate,
commission focused subject investigations through the coordinator, each the
author's sole substantive research assignment in a separate working context. An
existing context already dedicated to that subject may continue. Give each author
the full problem and constraints, its subject question and boundaries, relevant
primary-source leads and factual context, and the relationships it must resolve
with adjacent subjects. Preserve the initial accounts as discovery evidence;
the lead retains the whole problem, relationships between subjects, and subjects
not yet investigated. Use the scientific question as the investigation's target,
without passing a settled integrated plan or acceptance verdict as that target.
The coordinator may schedule subjects sequentially within the existing shared
allowance and staffing limits. Adequate existing research is reused; routine
questions need no such division.

A subject investigator develops the scientific explanation and its evidence
before producing a compact integration handoff. Choose follow-up questions from
the literature, compare materially different explanations and observations, and
perform useful bounded quantitative or observational research checks. Develop
mechanisms and limitations well enough to reveal approaches beyond the current
design; useful explanations need not already justify a named implementation
choice. Pursue useful follow-ups within the shared allowance, requesting permitted
support through the coordinator, without waiting for the user or main chat to
supply missing science. Preserve the objective, evidence and limits across
continuations. When source access fails, choose an authorized alternative or a
comparably informative discriminator and retain the remaining boundary. Return
an adequately developed subject account or an explicit partial account with the
remaining scientific work and actual limiting dependency. The lead integrates
the subject accounts after that work, preserves their detailed support and
conditions, and routes unresolved relationships or corrections to their authors.
Existing independent scientific review judges the accounts and their relationships
against the original scope. Keep material feasible scientific questions open and
owned even when the next engineering step is ready. The engineering owner owns
the implementation plan and takes up the integrated findings; the task owner
retains responsibility through scientific correction and uptake.

For broad grounding, establish a coverage contract across the whole requested
operating envelope: material domains and subcases, competing explanations,
evidence needed and the downstream decisions they affect. Require substantive
explanation and discriminating evidence within each important domain; excellent
treatment of one cannot compensate for an omitted or shallow other domain.
Where quantitative conclusions carry the design, perform appropriate bounded
derivations, reference calculations or public-observation checks instead of
only proposing future tests. Preserve the difference between these research
checks and product execution or qualification. Independent synthesis should
identify unsupported claims and missing depth, return useful gaps for correction,
and retain original versions. A broad task is not complete merely because its
topic headings, bibliography or initial handoff are complete.
Budget for broad discovery, primary-source reading, synthesis, counterevidence
and useful follow-up passes; use coordinator-dispatched independent branches
when they add coverage. A short scout allowance or compact message to the owner
must not silently become the depth limit for the whole investigation. Preserve
detailed reusable findings beneath the compact handoff. Independent audits,
settled implementation and preparation can continue while the lead works; hold
only commitments that actually depend on unresolved science. Research need not
be the user's only request, or the main chat's only useful activity.

Use a deeper scientific investigation when the user requests broad literature
grounding, or when competing mechanisms, uncertain empirical assumptions,
unfamiliar algorithms or consequential numerical tradeoffs could change the
development direction. A routine, settled edit needs no literature campaign.
Scale depth to the requested breadth, uncertainty and consequence; do not reduce
an explicitly comprehensive request to a few convenient papers. Allocate a
finite, useful budget and coverage across independent questions, then revisit
material gaps. Neither one search pass nor a long bibliography establishes
sufficiency. This guidance adds no compulsory research barrier before independent
implementation or ready expert judgment.

For native scientific authorship, research leadership and independent scientific
critique, use `sol_researcher` when the role is available in the running chat and
its `gpt-6.1-sol` / `ultra` pin is authorized. Source registration does not prove
actual tool or role availability.
This lean registered role owns scientific understanding and its evidence, not
implementation, architecture approval or the main chat's completion decision.
Registration grants no model permission or automatic escalation. If the role is
unavailable, or an inherited-only or other harder boundary excludes its pin, use
only an eligible supported responsibility, such as `inherited_reviewer`. Report
that the dedicated role was not delivered and identify the actual route and
settings; do not substitute a stronger model to obtain it.
The controller retains its existing responsibilities and uniform run-selected
model routing; this native role is not a controller responsibility or evidence
that controller prompts deliver the same role.

The research lead compares mechanisms and owns cross-subject scientific synthesis,
retaining scientific authorship for material subjects it does not delegate. It
may conduct one inquiry and synthesize the two after their independent accounts
are preserved; retain each inquiry's evidence and limitations. Scientific critique
remains independent of the account's authors and substantive repairers.
The coordinator can give Luna separable literature discovery,
primary-source verification and current-code mapping, returning findings to the
same lead. Helpers request assistance through the coordinator, never spawn their
own team. Preserve the initial consultation, architecture and completion gates.

Read relevant existing research and appraisals first when available. Establish
their dates, inspected revisions, scope and evidence limits; their conclusions
are neither verified current implementation facts nor fresh source verification.
Use them to avoid rediscovery and find missing or contradictory evidence.
**`_ref/` and `_appraisal/` are user-curated destinations: do not create or modify
their contents without an explicit request to curate those destinations.** An
older report proposing those paths does not supply that authorization. Keep
substantive agent-gathered scientific knowledge in an authorized `research/`
location or existing task evidence; retain detailed explanations and source
locators that later development can retrieve. Use temporary storage for search
scraps. Resolve the output destination against the authorized project before
writing, especially when studying another read-only checkout. This grants no
additional write permission, requires no new document for
every task and creates no parallel assignment ledger.

Build a task-specific map of scientific questions, approach families, influential
assumptions and important gaps before converging on a favorite method. Start from
the original outcome and actual operating conditions. Work forward through the
system and backward from the decisions and observable outcomes. Identify where
changed conditions, competing mechanisms, measurement limits or failed assumptions
could materially change a recommendation, including consequential combinations
and absence cases. Named examples and the first branch assignments are starting
points; retain important questions that cross branches or lie outside the
proposed design. Search
underlying mechanisms and adjacent terminology as well as project labels.
Consult foundational theory, original measurements and recent academic work;
selectively follow references backward and citations forward where they can
change coverage or expose counterevidence. Record the actual search scope,
search/publication dates and meaningful exclusions. Publication, observation and
web crawl dates are different. An unsuccessful bounded search does not establish
that no relevant work exists. Seek evidence that weakens the preferred approach
and alternatives that may be simpler or complementary.

Inspect relevant primary-source sections for consequential claims. Keep the
claim, source identity/link and locator, access level, supporting observation,
assumptions and application limits together. Distinguish measured, standardized,
derived, proposed, extrapolated and unresolved results; verify publication status
and identify preprints. Abstracts or secondary summaries do not establish unseen
methods, table values or validation. Preserve units, numerical definitions,
populations, operating regimes and uncertainty. Check whether reported statistics
describe separate marginals or observed joint events; marginal percentiles do not
establish co-occurrence or a joint distribution. Reconcile apparent disagreements
using those conditions, or preserve the genuine conflict. A standard test model,
one severe episode or a synthetic stress does not establish an environmental
distribution or universal bound. Blocked access leaves a claim unresolved unless
an authorized alternative supplies the evidence.

When a source contains both predictions and observations, inspect its results and
limitations as well as the model setup. Carry the actual comparison and its
measurement conventions into the decision; do not substitute assumed inputs or
predicted performance for measured outcomes, or omit contrary measured results.
Reconcile disagreements between a source's reported number and an independent
reconstruction, retaining both and the unresolved inputs when necessary.
Where a quantity controls a choice, follow its inputs, conventions and uncertainty
through to the engineering observable, then execute a feasible comparison that
could change the choice. For empirical claims, compare actual observations under
contrasting conditions or methods and preserve what makes the comparison valid.
If the preferred source or method is unavailable, pursue an authorized comparison
that can inform the same decision when feasible. Otherwise state the specific
missing input, what was tried and which judgment remains open.

Compare materially different approaches by mechanism, assumptions, practical
benefits, failure conditions, integration/resource cost and the evidence that
would distinguish them. Check mathematical or operational equivalence with
established methods and existing project capabilities before proposing another
implementation. Identify what is actually new, useful combinations, and the
remaining gap when equivalence is only partial. Neither a novel label nor a more
elaborate model establishes improvement. Retain supported positive, negative and
conditional findings, including when a rejected approach merits reconsideration.

Keep the detailed research reusable, with a compact decision summary pointing
into it. For consequential findings, carry **source → mechanism/conditions →
development decision → affected code or experiment → discriminating check**.
State a disposition such as reuse, adapt, test, reject, defer or unresolved, its
reason, and expected observations. Separate source support, design recommendation,
implemented behavior, executed checks and project qualification. Preserve current
code identity and actual available entry points; do not invent commands or turn
a proposed experiment into an observed result. This can be a short table or the
task's existing evidence format, not a mandatory new record system.

A design can be ready for a bounded next step while its scientific grounding
still has material gaps. Assess those judgments separately in the existing
independent review. For broad research, the existing staged scientific critic
begins with bounded literature discovery across the full research brief before receiving either
inquiry's question map, account or engineering plan. Using permitted evidence
routes and the shared allowance, inspect relevant primary work and citation
trails, then preserve source-supported explanations, competing approaches,
transfer limits and resulting questions in the existing initial scope, including
any changes to its framing. Reuse adequate supplied primary evidence; record
unresolved scope or missing access without bypassing tool, model or supplied-context
restrictions. After this checkpoint, provide the scientific account, or both
preserved inquiry accounts when paired, the continuing authored accounts, their
reconciliation and factual source context, **keeping engineering plans and prior
approvals withheld through scientific disposition**. Factual context excludes
engineering recommendations,
including suggestions appended to code observations. Do not ask this scientific
reviewer to approve architecture first. If an early
architecture decision needs review, use the existing separate permitted
responsibility within the same limits, or defer the dependent commitment.
Scientific accounts retain practical source-to-decision implications; the
reviewer's question is whether the original scientific problem is explained and
supported, not whether a first implementation tranche can begin.
This stages the existing scientific review without another recursive main-chat gate.
Reconcile important omissions and weak alternatives, primary evidence, decisive
quantitative comparisons and adverse or coupled cases. Return feasible scientific
follow-through with its impact and specific limits. If the account or plan was
already seen, disclose the actual exposure rather than claiming independent
initial scoping or protected adjudication; request suitable independent review
through the existing coordinator where feasible and preserve any remaining limit.

In the lead's reconciliation, retain each material question or justified
equivalent group from the inquiries and critic, including questions without a
supported conclusion. State each conclusion's conditions and unresolved
explanatory distinctions, and map the performed evidence to the distinctions it
actually resolves. A successful example closes only those
distinctions; a broader question remains open unless other evidence addresses the
consequential alternatives and establishes or bounds transfer across its relevant
conditions. Preserve
newly discovered questions, disagreements and reasons for removing an initial
question. No separate assignment ledger or source-count target is needed.
Before accepting a deployment or calibration boundary, check whether deeper
inspection of already relevant sources or a permitted representative calculation
or observation comparison can resolve the scientific distinction without the
missing target inputs. Have the continuing author complete that feasible work and
return changed evidence for review; if a real limit prevents it, retain the
specific unresolved conclusion, missing prerequisite and downstream consequence
rather than closing its broader question. Preserve earlier findings. Close broad
grounding when material questions have supported explanations across the requested
envelope or specific evidenced boundaries, with their consequences for development
clear. A scout return, plausible plan or incomplete synthesis remains intermediate
while material feasible research is outstanding. This uses the existing review
and dispatch process, without another recursive gate, universal team shape or
model permission. After scientific disposition and necessary changed-evidence review,
check that the engineering handoff takes up the reconciled accounts and limits.
Routine settled work still uses proportionate verification.

Before declaring research sufficient, independently cross-check coverage against
the original outcome and requested operating conditions, not just the selected
algorithm or accessible papers. Consider relevant physical mechanisms,
environment/regime, measurement, implementation/operating practice and validation.
Existing curated research can reveal missing branches without becoming an
unquestioned answer key. For each consequential omission, investigate it, explain
why it cannot change this decision, or retain a concrete unresolved prerequisite.
Primary technical recommendations, measurement reports and documented operating
evidence may complement academic papers; distinguish their authority and transfer
limits. Resolve useful gaps before repeating support for a settled central
recommendation. This is a task-specific coverage check, not a universal checklist
or a claim of exhaustive systematic review; a report with important open branches
can be a useful intermediate result without fulfilling the whole research request.

During audit, planning, implementation and review, actively retrieve and use the
relevant research; a citation in a plan is not evidence that code realizes it.
Workers receive the decision, applicability limits and source/check pointers,
then inspect current source and exercise the authorized implementation path.
Reviewers check consequential uptake and whether new evidence changes the
recommendation. Reopen the relevant research when an assumption fails, gains vary
by regime, an equivalent capability appears, or a measurement/implementation gap
could change the next decision. Reconcile old and new results without erasing
failures or repeating an unchanged broad review. Routine edits need no ceremonial
citation. Within the original scientific scope, stop research at adequate
coverage, diminishing useful returns or a real limit, with unresolved work
explicit; research completion does not finish an outstanding implementation
request.

All of this remains subject to the actual tools, model boundary and assignment
authority. Controller profiles retain their no-network restriction and the
supplied-context profile retains its no-tools instruction: use supplied or
authorized local evidence and request missing external research from the
coordinator, without fetching it or bypassing a hold. Do not assume installing
prompt text creates browsing capability. Prompt-delivery checks establish wiring,
not compliance, research quality, token savings or equivalence to historical
multi-model research campaigns.

> below supplies the application, operating envelope, constraints and factual

> research as a dated starting point. If assigned one of two independent full

> do not read the other inquiry's map/findings or an emerging engineering plan
> before the coordinator's initial-account checkpoint. Preserve your substantive
> first account at this discovery checkpoint. The lead then derives scientific
> subjects from the problem and inspected evidence. Inadequately grounded subjects
> receive focused investigations, each the author's sole substantive research
> assignment in a separate working context; an already dedicated context may
> continue. Retain the full problem, constraints and adjacent-subject relationships.
> Develop the subject account before a compact integration handoff; the lead
> integrates accounts and retains unresolved relationships. Reuse adequate

> Reconcile its claims with current code and new positive, negative or conditional
